rationale: The hypothesis posits that pediatric-onset SNUPN deficiency consistently represents an atypical, multisystem muscular dystrophy distinct from classical isolated limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD), characterized by early neurological and neurodevelopmental defects. While large pediatric cohorts (such as Nashabat et al. reporting 18 pediatric patients across 15 families) describe syndromic/complex presentations with prominent neurological co-morbidities, other pivotal studies directly contradict this generalization. Specifically, Iruzubieta et al. (2024) characterized 5 patients with homozygous SNUPN mutations presenting with a childhood-onset, non-syndromic limb-girdle muscular dystrophy phenotype characterized by proximal muscle weakness, restrictive respiratory impairment, contractures, and myofibrillar-like pathology on biopsy without mandatory early neurodevelopmental co-morbidities. Furthermore, Muelas et al. (2026) explicitly observe that SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy (LGMDR29) spans a phenotypic continuum ranging from pure childhood-onset muscular dystrophy to complex phenotypes combining neurodevelopmental deficits, cataracts, or spinocerebellar ataxia, alongside adult-onset presentations. Hence, the hypothesis that pediatric-onset disease is uniformly an atypical multisystem syndrome rather than capable of presenting as isolated/pure LGMD is conflicted.

evidence.text: Five patients from two unrelated families carrying a biallelic SNUPN variant (p.Ile309Ser) demonstrated a limb-girdle muscular dystrophy phenotype according to current definitions, characterized by childhood-onset proximal weakness, restrictive respiratory dysfunction, and prominent contractures without obligatory syndromic neurodevelopmental impairment.

source.title: Biallelic variants in SNUPN cause a limb girdle muscular dystrophy with myofibrillar-like features
source.quote: Here, we present five patients from two unrelated families with a limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD) phenotype carrying a biallelic variant in SNUPN gene. ... evidence.text: LGMDR29 spans a wide phenotypic spectrum that covers from congenital or childhood-onset pure muscular dystrophy to complex syndromic phenotypes combining neurodevelopmental features, cataracts, or spinocerebellar ataxia, as well as late-onset presentations.

source.quote: SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy or LGMDR29 is a new entity that covers from a congenital or childhood onset pure muscular dystrophy to more complex phenotypes combining neurodevelopmental features, cataracts, or spinocerebellar ataxia. So far, 12 different variants have been described. Here we report the first family with SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy presenting an adult-onset myopathy as well as novel ultrastructural findings.

source.quote: Mutations in the SNUPN gene, which encodes snurportin-1, a nuclear import adaptor for U1 small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNP), have recently been implicated in limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, attributed to disrupted pre-messenger RNA splicing in skeletal muscle. ... We identified pathogenic variants in the SNUPN gene in two families with spinocerebellar atrophy. One patient exhibited mild changes in skeletal muscle, while the other did not.

conflicts: Iruzubieta et al. (2024) demonstrate that childhood-onset SNUPN mutations (e.g., p.Ile309Ser) can cause a pure/isolated limb-girdle muscular dystrophy phenotype with myofibrillar features, devoid of mandatory syndromic or severe neurodevelopmental impairment, directly conflicting with the premise that pediatric SNUPN deficiency is universally distinct from classical isolated LGMD.

Muelas et al. (2026) explicitly define LGMDR29 as spanning a spectrum from pure childhood-onset muscular dystrophy to syndromic entities with neurodevelopmental features, cataracts, or ataxia, contradicting any categorical dichotomization of pediatric SNUPN deficiency as exclusively multisystemic.

new_directions.question_text: Do specific SNUPN domain disruptions (such as importin-beta-binding domain versus snRNP cap-binding domain mutations) correlate with isolated myopathic versus complex multisystem/neurodevelopmental phenotypes?
new_directions.rationale: Identifying distinct genotype-phenotype correlations will clarify why some variants cause pure childhood LGMD while others produce multisystem neurological disease.

new_directions.question_text: What tissue-specific alternative splicing targets in the central nervous system versus skeletal muscle account for the divergent clinical manifestations of biallelic SNUPN variants?
new_directions.rationale: Comparative transcriptomic profiling across human iPSC-derived cerebellar neurons and skeletal myocytes will resolve the molecular drivers of phenotypic pleiotropy.
